transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 16:30 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Heather Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (Quantile Head of Search), Lena Moore (Quantile ML), Alexei Voronov (Quantile CTO), Priya Shah (Quantile Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, noisy):
Quantile is evaluating Redwood for a retrieval + rerank pipeline. Primary concerns: throughput at 500-2k QPS for embeddings lookups, tail latency under 120ms for retrieval+rerank, on-prem / VPC security and KMS integration, and operational model for reindex/refresh. They want to compare Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with a small pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Heather Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, happy holidays too i guess, this is Heather from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. Diego, SE, will cover the deep tech bits after a quick context check.
[00:17] Sanjay Patel: Thanks Heather. Quick context from our side, Quantile Health — we run a large docs search for clinical guidance and internal notes. We're looking at retrieval + reranking, and want to move off our prototype (open-source vector store + a lambda-based reranker) into something more predictable for production.
[00:32] Lena Moore: yeah we have about 40 million docs total, currently index ~8M for pilot, embedded at 1536 dims using OpenAI-like embeddings. Our main worries: throughput for bulk inference during reindex, and per-request latency when we do reranking (cross-encoder).
[00:45] Alexei Voronov: also for compliance we may need VPC or on-prem, and we require KMS with customer-managed keys.
[00:52] Heather Park: that's great context. Diego, want to kick off with how Redwood typically fits into an embedding + rerank pipeline?
[00:58] Diego Ramos: yeah thanks. So typical Redwood flow — you have embeddings for retrieval and an optional cross-encoder reranker. For embedding store we integrate with vector DBs or can serve embeddings from Redwood and run hybrid search. For rerank we often recommend a small dedicated GPU pool to keep tail latency consistent because cross-encoders are compute-heavy.
[01:18] Sanjay: quick question, when you say "integrate with vector DBs" — do you mean you can call out to existing Milvus/Pinecone clusters, or do you want us to migrate into Redwood's hosting?
[01:27] Diego: both. We support a few patterns: 1) Redwood-hosted embeddings + Redwood search layer that does ANN and hybrid topk (good for quick pilots). 2) Redwood as a model-serving layer only where we return embeddings and you store them in your vector DB (like Milvus). 3) Private deployment where we run the inference and the routing inside your VPC and we can sit next to your DB.
[01:45] Priya Shah: security — what about audit logs and access controls? We need RBAC and long-term audit retention (7 years ideally).
[01:53] Heather: we have audit logs and RBAC in Redwood Console; for Private we can forward logs to your SIEM and integrate with KMS/HSM for encryption at rest. Diego will follow up with the specific compliance doc.
[02:08] Lena: on embeddings dims — we use 1536 dims currently, but we are exploring 768 to save storage and speed up ANN. Any guidance there?
[02:18] Diego: tradeoff is signal vs cost. For clinical text, higher dims tend to preserve nuance but you can get good results with 768 depending on your encoder. We often run a quick eval — compute recall@k and downstream rerank delta. For throughput: 768 embeddings are smaller, lower network and index CPU. Also quantization helps if you host on Dedicated/private.
[02:40] Sanjay: rerank architecture — we use a two-stage: vector retrieval for top 100, then cross-encoder rerank top 10. Does Redwood support batching of reranker calls and prefix caching? Latency is key for us.
[02:52] Diego: yes, we support continuous batching and KV cache at the runtime layer. Rerankers are batched on GPU pools; for tail SLO we size dedicated pools and colocate reranker with the model to avoid network hops. Cache is more for generative prefix but we do have token/KV-like caching for some transformer rerankers when requests share prefixes — less common for cross-encoders, but for rerank you can cache previous rerank results for identical query-doc pairs.
[03:20] Alexei: about throughput — we expect spikes around 2k qps for search during peak hours; typical sustained is 800-1200 qps. We need a plan for autoscale or burst.
[03:33] Diego: Dedicated pools are good for predictable throughput; you get reserved GPU capacity and autoscale policies with burst buckets. Hosted will work for lower steady-state, but tail latency may vary under noisy neighbors. For strict SLOs and regulatory needs, Private with reserved pools in your VPC is common.
[03:50] Sanjay: reindex throughput — when we do full re-embed 8M docs, what does that look like? We don't want full jobs taking days.
[03:59] Diego: depends on batch size and ML infra. With Redwood Dedicated on A10s or H100s you can push embeddings at 50-200k docs/hour per GPU depending on model/seq lengths. We also support incremental updates so you don't need full reindex every time. We have a bulk ingest API and parallel workers. We'll share a benchmark sheet.
[04:20] Priya: encryption and keys — do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys? Also SSO/SAML for user provisioning?
[04:29] Heather: yes to both. Private has options to connect to your KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault) and we can use HSM-backed keys in some enterprise plans. SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning is supported. Diego will attach the security pack.
[04:43] Lena: curious about vector DB sharding — if we keep our existing Milvus cluster and we do cross-DC reads, any guidance for topology?
[04:52] Diego: for large corpuses we recommend sharding by logical partition (e.g., tenant or timeframe) and pinning high-QPS shards on dedicated nodes. For hybrid search we do a fanout to ANN then apply rerank. Tail latency is the sum of ANN + network + rerank. So colocating reranker near DB or using Redwood private routing reduces network cost.
[05:15] Sanjay: ok and what about incremental reindex / consistency? We have frequent doc updates and need near real-time updates in the index.
[05:23] Diego: we support upserts and small-object diffs; you can stream embeddings into Redwood or push embeddings to your DB. For private deploy we can run a small worker next to DB that picks up changes and updates the index. We also have configurable eventual consistency windows to prioritize availability.
[05:40] Alexei: do you have customers running strict PII workloads fully on-prem? That would be a hard requirement for some lines of our business.
[05:48] Heather: yes, several healthcare customers run Redwood Private on-prem or in VPC-only setups. We can provide references and an on-prem checklist. That involves packaging the control plane locally or using a private control plane option.
[06:05] Sanjay: pricing — ballpark for dedicated pools for 2 GPUs reserved vs hosted per-token/call pricing? We need a simple comparison to justify commit.
[06:14] Heather: we'll send a side-by-side: hosted usage-based, dedicated reserved monthly + usage, private licensing for on-prem + support. For your numbers we can model cost per query given 1536 dims retrieval + cross-encoder rerank and show breakpoints where dedicated becomes cheaper.
[06:30] Lena: one last tech nit — we use vector quantization in the index sometimes for storage; any interoperability issues?
[06:38] Diego: quantization is in the index layer; Redwood can ingest and return embeddings unchanged. For on-the-fly quantized models it's more about inference precision. For reranking, we recommend not quantizing the reranker weights (keep FP16/FP32 on GPU) to preserve accuracy. For retrieval indexes you can use PQ/OPQ. We'll share recommended settings.
[06:56] Sanjay: sounds good. Next steps then?
[07:01] Heather: recap: Heather to send pricing and pilot template; Diego to share private deploy network diagram + security pack; Lena to upload sample dataset; schedule a benchmark session in early Jan. Any other blockers?
[07:13] Priya: we'll run a quick compliance Q&A with your security doc — if all good, we can proceed.
[07:20] Alexei: we'll loop in infra to sign off on network.
[07:24] Heather: perfect, thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links. Happy holidays!
